## Critique examples

### 1. Agent's 404 claim was wrong for real browser requests: `next.config.ts`, commits `a52175b` → `6ab5eea`
- **What the agent proposed:** After building `/projects/[slug]`, Viber reported "all routes 200, `/projects/unknown-slug` → 404" and left `cacheComponents: true` in the config.
- **Decision:** Rejected the claim and asked for a fix. A user's browser sends GET, so the GET status is the one that matters.
- **Why:** With Cache Components and partial prerendering, the page shell starts streaming before `notFound()` runs, so the status is already 200. The page *looks* like a 404 but isn't one.
- **Check and actual outcome:** Built the app (`next build && next start`) and requested `/projects/abc`, `/projects/unknown-slug` and `/projects/product-inventory-cli`. **Before the fix:** GET returned **200** for both unknown slugs (body contained "Project not found"); only `curl -I` (HEAD) returned 404. **After the fix (`6ab5eea`):** Viber's GET check returned `/projects/abc` → **404**, `product-inventory-cli` → 200, `urban-logistics-optimization` → 200.

### 2. Silent data-loss risk in the JSON store: `lib/contact/store.ts`, commit `f590402`
- **What the agent proposed:** `readSubmissions()` wrapped `readFile` in `try { … } catch { return { submissions: [] } }`, treating every read error as "file doesn't exist yet".
- **Decision:** Changed it so only `ENOENT` means "start with an empty list". Any other error is rethrown, so the Server Action returns the save-error message.
- **Why:** If the file exists but can't be read (a permissions or I/O error), the old code would write `[newSubmission]` over it and silently delete every earlier submission.
- **Check and actual outcome:** Read the updated code: the `catch` now rethrows unless `code === "ENOENT"`. Viber added a test that makes the file unreadable and confirmed the save now throws instead of overwriting; the test passed.

### 3. Submissions file excluded from the repository: `.gitignore`, commit `f590402`
- **What the agent proposed:** Added `/data` to `.gitignore`, so neither the folder nor `contact-submissions.json` was committed.
- **Decision:** Changed it to commit an empty `data/contact-submissions.json` (`[]`) and ignore only `data/*.corrupt-*.json` and `data/*.tmp`.
- **Why:** The assignment requires saving submissions to a JSON file. Reviewers should see where that file lives and what it looks like, while backup and temp files stay out of git.
- **Check and actual outcome:** `git show --stat f590402` lists `data/contact-submissions.json` (content `[]`). `.gitignore` now ignores only the backup and temp patterns.

## Independent end-to-end check of the contact form
After the form was written, I ran a separate end-to-end check: a production build, then real form POSTs to `/contact-me-server-form` with the page's own hidden action fields (the same request a browser sends without JavaScript). Results:
- Valid (`Mars`, `mars@example.com`, `hello`) → "Thanks! Your message has been sent successfully." Exactly **1** record was written, with `id`, `name`, `email`, `message`, `createdAt` and `source: "server-form"`.
- Name of only spaces → "Name is required."
- `a@b` and `a@b..com` → "Email must include a valid domain after the @ (e.g. example.com)."
- `a b@c.com` → "Email must not contain whitespace."
- `a@@b.com` → "Email must contain exactly one @."
- Message of only spaces → "Message is required."
- The page renders `<label for>` for `name`, `email` and `message`.

## Critique examples

### 1. JSON bodies with wrong types would have crashed the contact API: `app/api/contact/route.ts`, commit `2876688`
- **What the agent proposed:** In the planning step, reuse `validateContactForm` unchanged for the JSON API.
- **Decision:** Accepted the reuse but changed the input handling. Each field is converted to a string (or `""`) before validation. Later, this coercion moved into `stringField()` in `lib/http.ts` (`ca9dc70`).
- **Why:** `FormData` always gives strings, but JSON doesn't. `validateContactForm` calls `.trim()`, so `{"name": 123}` would throw and return a 500 instead of a 400 validation error.
- **Check and actual outcome:** Viber's curl test with `{"name":123,"email":"x@y.co","message":"hi"}` returned **400** `{"ok":false,"errors":{"name":"Name is required."}}`. Blank name → 400, `a@b` → 400, non-JSON → 400 "Request body must be valid JSON.", valid body → **201** with `source: "api"`.

### 2. Repeated copy-paste in agent-generated code: `components/formStyles.ts`, `lib/jsonFile.ts`, `lib/http.ts`, `lib/blogs/useBlogPosts.ts`, commits `b17d967`, `4dd7dab`, `ca9dc70`, `11fe860`
- **What the agent proposed:** Each new feature copied an existing pattern instead of reusing it: form styles, the JSON file queue / read / write logic, the request-parsing block, and the list-fetching effect.
- **Decision:** Rejected the duplication four times and asked for one shared module each time, with behavior unchanged.
- **Why:** The rubric (A2.2-06) penalizes unexplained duplicate logic. Duplicated store code is also risky: a fix to one copy (such as the ENOENT rethrow from Part 1) could silently be missing from the other.
- **Check and actual outcome:** After each refactor, build and lint passed and the earlier tests were re-run: the blog data tests passed, and contact POST still returned 201 while blogs POST returned 201 and a blank title returned 400. In my browser check, `/admin/blogs` and `/blogs` show the same list from the shared `BlogPostList`.

### 3. Agent's curl tests missed a browser-only failure, and my first theory about it was wrong: environment, no code commit
- **What happened:** All of Viber's checks used curl. When I opened `http://localhost:3000/blogs` in a real browser, the page stayed on "Loading posts...", and the network log showed **900+ `GET /api/blogs` requests in a few seconds**, all 200, with no console errors.
- **Decision:** Asked Viber to investigate before changing any code. I suggested a theory: running `npm run build` while `npm run dev` was running had broken the dev output in `.next`.
- **Why:** The hook's effect only depends on `reloadKey`, so the code didn't look like it could loop. Changing it blindly could have hidden the real cause.
- **Agent's findings:** My exact theory was **partly wrong**: Next 16 writes dev output to a separate `.next/dev` folder. But the Turbopack cache in `.next/cache/turbopack` is shared. The dev server had started at 18:59, the same minute as a `npm run build`, and its log showed modules compiled as "The module has no exports at all", **15,622 full page reloads**, and ongoing recompiles every ~150–200 ms with no browser open. Each reload remounted `/blogs` and fired another fetch.
- **Check and actual outcome:** I stopped the dev server, ran `rm -rf .next` and `npm run dev`. In my browser check: `/blogs` made **2** requests (the React StrictMode double-run) and showed "No posts yet."; `/admin/blogs` showed "Title is required." and "Content is required." for a blank submission, then "Post created!" with the new post listed immediately; `/blogs/test-post-from-admin` showed the post with its line breaks; `/blogs/nope` returned **HTTP 404** "Post not found"; `/blog-posts` redirected to `/blogs`; `/contact-me` showed all three field errors (POST → **400**), then "Thanks! Your message has been sent successfully." (POST → **201**), and the record appeared in `data/contact-submissions.json` with `source: "api"`. Lesson: don't run `npm run build` in the same folder while `npm run dev` is running.
